Score sites with CTAS

Analyze_CTAS.Rd

A gsm-friendly wrapper around ctas::process_a_study(). It takes a single long data frame in the CTAS + ctasapp vocabulary (typically the output of an Input_*() function), splits by study when the multi-study contract is active, runs process_a_study() per study, and returns the flat results frame ctasapp displays.

Usage

Analyze_CTAS(
  dfInput,
  bAutocorr = TRUE,
  bAverage = TRUE,
  bSD = TRUE,
  bRange = FALSE,
  bUniqueValueCountRelative = TRUE,
  bOwnSiteSimilScore = FALSE,
  bLOF = FALSE,
  nMinTimepoints = 1,
  nMinSubjects = 3,
  dMaxShareMissing = 0.5,
  bChangeFromBaseline = FALSE,
  bAutogenerate = TRUE,
  strScoringMethod = "ks",
  strPadjustMethod = "fdr",
  dfCustomTimeseries = ctas::ctas_data$custom_timeseries,
  dfCustomReferenceGroups = ctas::ctas_data$custom_reference_groups,
  nSeed = NULL,
  strStudyCol = "studyid",
  ...
)

Arguments

dfInput

data.frame Long-format CTAS input with at minimum subject_id, site, parameter_id, parameter_name, parameter_category_1/2/3, timepoint_1_name, timepoint_2_name, timepoint_rank, result, baseline. Additional CTAS subject columns (country, region) are carried through when present.

bAutocorr

logical Score the autocorr feature.

bAverage

logical Score the average feature.

bSD

logical Score the sd feature.

bRange

logical Score the range feature.

bUniqueValueCountRelative

logical Score the unique_value_count_relative feature.

bOwnSiteSimilScore

logical Score the own_site_simil_score feature.

bLOF

logical Score the lof feature.

nMinTimepoints

numeric Minimum timepoints per timeseries.

nMinSubjects

numeric Minimum subjects per timeseries.

dMaxShareMissing

numeric Maximum share of missing timepoints.

bChangeFromBaseline

logical Derive change-from-baseline timeseries.

bAutogenerate

logical Autogenerate timeseries.

strScoringMethod

character One of "ks", "mixedeffects", "avg_feat_value".

strPadjustMethod

character Passed to stats::p.adjust().

dfCustomTimeseries

data.frame Custom timeseries table forwarded to ctas::process_a_study(). Defaults to the shipped ctas::ctas_data.

dfCustomReferenceGroups

data.frame Custom reference-group table forwarded to ctas::process_a_study(). Defaults to ctas::ctas_data$custom_reference_groups.

nSeed

numeric Optional seed for reproducibility.

strStudyCol

character Column on dfInput identifying the study. NULL disables the split and drops the study output column.

...

Further arguments passed to ctas::process_a_study().

Value

data.frame One row per (site x timeseries x feature), carrying parameter_id, the category columns, and study (when the multi-study contract is active).

Details

Only results is returned; the input and untransformed frames ctasapp also consumes are pure projections of the input dfInput, so the metric YAML assembles the ctasapp payload in a separate base::list step (see inst/workflow/2_metrics/*.yaml).

The single-df pattern follows ctasval: subjects and parameters are re-derived from dfInput via distinct() inside the function so callers only have to keep one frame consistent.

Feature selection is a boolean-per-feature contract instead of the semicolon-delimited string CTAS accepts, so metric YAMLs can toggle features individually from meta:.

Examples

# \donttest{
dfSubjects <- data.frame(
  studyid = pharmaversesdtm::dm$STUDYID,
  subject_id = pharmaversesdtm::dm$USUBJID,
  site = pharmaversesdtm::dm$SITEID,
  country = pharmaversesdtm::dm$COUNTRY
)
dfValues <- Standardize_Domain(
  dfDomain = pharmaversesdtm::vs,
  dfSubjects = dfSubjects,
  strTestCDCol = "VSTESTCD", strTestCol = "VSTEST",
  strValueCol = "VSSTRESN",
  strCategory = "Vital Signs"
)
dfResults <- Analyze_CTAS(dfValues, nSeed = 1)
#> Warning: There were 26 warnings in `mutate()`.
#> The first warning was:
#> ℹ In argument: `ts_features = list(...)`.
#> ℹ In row 5.
#> Caused by warning in `cor()`:
#> ! the standard deviation is zero
#> ℹ Run `dplyr::last_dplyr_warnings()` to see the 25 remaining warnings.
lAnalysis <- list(ID = "numeric", results = dfResults,
                  input = dfValues, untransformed = dfValues)
# }
